issues.quote: The regulator on the wall had stopped.
issues.fact: The fact sheet gives no information about the wall regulator or when it stopped.
issues.misreading: A solver could treat the stopped regulator as a time anchor, reading its stoppage as the moment of the death or of the blow, which the sheet does not support and which could conflict with the kitchen-clock readings.

issues.quote: His repeater was in his hand.
issues.fact: The fact sheet says nothing about the repeater's face or reading. It is a watch, and the transcript gives no time shown on it.
issues.misreading: A solver could look for a time on the repeater, or treat it as a second clock whose reading might be compared with the kitchen clock, when no such reading is given.

issues.quote: That old Morbier, it strikes by its own face. You can hear it all through the house.
issues.fact: The fact sheet says only that Rosa heard the hall clock strike eleven when her kitchen clock showed 11:03. It does not say the hall clock can be heard throughout the house or that it strikes by its own face.
issues.misreading: A solver could take the added audibility claim as a hint about whereabouts or about how far sound carried, which the sheet does not establish.
